learn.title: A line that cuts two lines
learn.body: Parallel lines never meet and stay the same distance apart. A transversal is a line that crosses two or more other lines. When it crosses two parallel lines, it makes eight angles that follow clear rules.

learn.title: The picture
learn.body: Two horizontal lines are parallel. A slanted line crosses both. Angle 1 is above the top line, right of the slant. Angle 2 is below the bottom line, left of the slant. Angles 3 and 4 are between the lines, 3 on the left and 4 on the right. Figure not to scale.
learn.alt: Two horizontal parallel lines crossed by a slanted line. Four angles are numbered 1 to 4 around the two crossing points.

learn.title: Four rules
learn.body: Corresponding angles are equal. Alternate interior angles are equal. Alternate exterior angles are equal. Same-side interior angles add to $180^\circ$. These hold only when the two lines really are parallel.

learn.title: Use the rules
learn.body: The lines are parallel. Find $x$ in each case.
Find one angle you know, then pass it around: equal to its corresponding or alternate partner, and supplementary to its neighbour on the line.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two corresponding angles are always what?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles sit in the same position at each crossing, so they are equal when the lines are parallel.

questions.prompt: Which pair of angles adds to $180^\circ$?
questions.explanation: The other three pairs are equal. Same-side interior angles are supplementary.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines. Two alternate interior angles are $(2x+5)^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. Find $x$.
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal: $2x+5=75$, so $x=35$.

questions.prompt: The top and bottom lines are parallel and angle 1 measures $50^\circ$. What does angle 4 measure?
questions.explanation: Angle 4 and angle 1 sit side by side across the top line, so they form a linear pair: $180-50=130$.
questions.alt: Two horizontal parallel lines crossed by a slanted line. Four angles are numbered 1 to 4 around the two crossing points.

questions.prompt: The top and bottom lines are parallel and angle 1 measures $50^\circ$. What does angle 2 measure in degrees?
questions.explanation: Angles 1 and 2 are alternate exterior angles, so they are equal.
questions.alt: Two horizontal parallel lines crossed by a slanted line. Four angles are numbered 1 to 4 around the two crossing points.

questions.explanation: Together they make a straight angle, so they add to $180^\circ$.

questions.prompt: Parallel lines. Same-side interior angles are $x^\circ$ and $(x+30)^\circ$. Find $x$.
